chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Bahr Al-Saqqa' has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Bahr Al-Saqqa', who is Bahr ibn Kathir.

key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ: Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.بَحْرِ السَّقَّاءِ: Bahr Al-Saqqa' (Bahr the Water-Seller), a companion of the Imams
key_terms.حَرِيزَ: Hariz, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it / I transmitted it
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a prominent narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator Bahr Al-Saqqa' and how is his chain of transmission verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to authenticate the specific transmission chain (isnad) for narrations attributed to Bahr al-Saqqa', clarifying that he personally received them from his father, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn. This establishes a direct scholarly link from the Imamate back to the companion Bahr ibn Kathir, reinforcing the reliability of the reports in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. The mention of 'Bahr al-Saqqa'' (the water-carrier) highlights the humble origins of this key narrator, a detail often noted in Shia biographical dictionaries to emphasize the accessibility of religious knowledge.
